reviews.title: Wonderful!
reviews.text: I have ADHD, OCD, and an anxiety disorder. So you could say that some days keeping myself taken care of can be difficult. This app has not only helped me with my daily tasks like taking medication or making my bed, but also extra goals and tasks I set for myself! Finch also has a great community and subreddit for you to go to if you’d like. When I first downloaded finch I wasn’t sure how it could help me, but knew it was an app worth trying after looking around and seeing that they have so many options to customize your bird to reflect who you are! Pride flags, mobility aids, and the ability to change the pronouns of the bird at anytime (so if you use them as a self reflection and are processing your own gender or lack there of, you can change it again and again) Finch is obviously very inclusive and its community is the same. I truly enjoy using the app and taking advantage of its meditation sounds, nature sounds, anxiety manga techniques and promos on reflection. Finch is absolutely worth giving a try if you find you are interested but unsure. They have free access which still gives you great things, and you can always decide to pay for it if you want even more options. I personally didn’t find I was missing that much when utilizing the free program! Having plus does give you more options that I take advantage too, and I think it’s a good price also. TLDR: I can keep my life and self care straight thanks to this app. Their community is great too.

reviews.title: This app helped me so much
reviews.text: I love love love this app. I was bedridden for a while because of mental health things and couldn’t even get out of bed. I downloaded this app and something about taking care of this bird motivated me. The app can make goals for you or you can make your own so I do both. Some of them are super simple, like “get out of bed” or “brush teeth” but just having some sort of reward for doing those things helped me so much. I was also able to build up to certain things that were overwhelming to me because of the depression, like having a conversation with at least one person during the day. I’m still going to use this app to help me build up to being able to hang out with friends/make plans. It’s the perfect app to do it with because you’re able to take it slow and take little steps if needed. I feel so responsible for this dang bird which is a good thing since it helped me take action, even if the actions are small. You also don’t get penalized/made to feel bad if you don’t complete some goals for your day which I really like. There’s no negative aspect to the app. It’s all encompassed in positivity and support. There’s a lot of other cool features and resources such as breath work to do if you have a panic attack (under a ‘first aid’ widget) or things such as yoga poses to do (even offering couch ones in case you don’t wanna/can’t get up). The app has weirdly helped me so much as I’m finding that I would do anything for this bird. Highly recommend trying it out!

reviews.title: Finch Community
reviews.text: I have to be honest with everyone, Finch does wonders. I first started Finch whenever I thought I was being lazy and not doing much. But slowly I realized it was actually a state of depression. I started using Finch with like everything, I mean EVERYTHING. Finch is an amazing app that doesn’t require any money for it to be great. Anyways, Finch’s community. Finch has such a great community built with it I am actually so grateful for all of it. I sent out a submission to get a subscription because I knew it would help. In a little amount of time I got feedback which was me getting one! I thought this was amazing and knew I could get better with myself. One day throughout it though I fell back. I went to being lazy and ignorant to a lot of people and things that I should do. But there was now something that I actually wanted. Which was Finch because now I had gotten blessed with something I wanted and I had a purpose to use it even more. After a month the subscription was up. I was a little saddened but then I saw I could refill it, but I’m broke.. So I pressed I couldn't afford it and got blessed again. So sorry for it being so long, but in summary. Finch and its community is like a whole family supporting each other. If you can help others you can easily do it with Finch. And if you’re someone who needs help, Finch has your back. 100% would recommend this app to literally anyone, struggling or not it’s worth your time. Thank for reading this rant message. lol

reviews.title: Truly a Life Saver
reviews.text: I spent 62 days in the hospital this year, many of them in the ICU for sepsis, and was left with short term memory struggles as well as no motivation to do anything or even be alive. I had the app years ago when it first came out but switched phones and never re-downloaded, but was reminded of it’s existence by a close friend. I downloaded again and have been so grateful for it. Before Finch, I was struggling to remember if i had brushed my teeth or washed my face or drank water, along with living in a constant state of panic. Now I’m consistently taking care of myself again and feeling good about it! I’ve never been the type of person that could get excited about self care and always struggled to form new habits, all of which was exacerbated by being brain-fried from being severely ill, however I am now waking up excited to take care of myself and talk to my little birdie each day. The app is beautifully designed, incredibly in-depth, and emotionally intelligent. I’ve found a community of people who instead of belittling you for your short comings or struggles encourages you and reminds you that you are not alone. Finch Plus has been worth every penny, though not absolutely necessary by any means, and I cannot appreciate that enough. Too often an app is only useful when paying for the premium version. I am so grateful to the Finch team, the app itself, and the community I’ve found. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. If you’re considering downloading, please do!

reviews.title: Finally something worked.
reviews.text: For years now, I’ve been struggling with a plethora of mental health issues on top of adhd, and it’s made it extremely difficult for me to take care of myself even with professional help. I’ve learned to take care of my emotions, but the motivation to do things has never been there for me especially with my adhd. Doing things like going and getting a cup of water, washing my face, getting clothes off the floor or bringing bowls and plates down from my room has always been something that’s felt genuinely impossible. On top of all of that even, I’ve never had any motivation to stretch or work out. I’ve downloaded so many of these apps and they’ve all just been gimmicky and overpriced, and I’ve found they only made me feel worse because the reminders felt pointless and made me feel like I didn’t care about myself. With Finch, i not only feel reinforced that I care about myself, I also feel cared for by my finch, and I feel that by taking care of myself, im also taking care of him. In the past few days, I’ve done so much more with this app then I ever thought. Im really happy that I finally have some motivational help that actually works. I absolutely love finch and I actually couldn’t recommend it more. Also, I’d like to mention that I haven’t reviewed an app for like four years now because there’s never been an app that I cared for like this. I’m really happy to use this app and I want you to try it if you’re reading this.

reviews.title: Finch is My Bestie
reviews.text: Finch is the ultimate To Do list app. With the ability to create my own tasks and how often they pop up, and the rewards I earn by doing simple things for myself like smiling in the mirror or folding my laundry, I feel much more secure in my ability to take care of myself and remember to keep things kind and tidy. The app has breathing exercises, self affirmation exercises, a customizable checklist of tasks, and the ability to team up with friends to hold each-other accountable for a linked task. All of the above earns you rewards in either energy or the in game currency, which has no sleazy way to “pay to win.” The only option for in app purchases are to buy premium or buy someone else premium by sponsoring a fellow Finch user. The currency you earn can be spent on apparel, home decor, or new colors for your finch’s plumage! On a personal note, this app has been there for me through some of my deepest depressions and biggest moments of grief. When the people in my life can’t lift me up for whatever reason, I still have Finch in my pocket to help me be the support I need. Additionally, when my life has been so hectic that I couldn’t hear myself think, I was able to pause my app so my streaks didn’t disappear. As someone that personally struggles on an extreme level with daily tasks and habits, this has actually been life changing for me. I hope more developers take note and make more gamified self care apps that actually feel rewarding.

reviews.title: You saved my daughter
reviews.text: It’s been 108 days for her and I believe 103 (?) for me and my oldest daughter downloaded the app 45 days ago. We be dealt with a lot in the past 4 years. Life changing health issues, identity theft, the loss of our dog, my townhome and my job and most recently my car. We’re living in a motel and the depression has been off the charts. My youngest found your app and downloaded it and told me about it 4 days later. It has made such a difference in our lives. She went from sleeping 20 hours a day to completing tasks to take care of herself and her birb. She encourages me and her sister as well. It’s helped me get back on track with my own issues and focusing on getting us out of here and into a home. Both of my girls are chronically ill and have been for years. Having this app gives them direction that they can choose and work on without having to tell anyone or talk about it if they don’t want to. They’re both introverts so this is perfect. In October, my youngest (Olivia) was chosen by the Guardians for the plus package and she just lit up when she found out. She has had so much fun with her birb and I’ve noticed her adding goals to her list and making noticeable changes for herself. I’m so grateful to you for creating this app. She’s a brain tumor survivor and this is the first time I’ve seen her make positive decisions for herself in years. When I’m able, I would love to be a Guardian so I can pay it forward. From my heart, thank you 💜

reviews.title: This app is 100% worth it
reviews.text: I’m not one to write reviews but this is 100% worth it. It makes it fun to accomplish goals every day, and I’m actually doing things consistently that I’ve been trying to get in the habit of for months. It offers exercises, stretches, wellness quizzes, soundscapes, writing prompts, acts of kindness, and of course, your goals. It even has an entire section dedicated to panic attacks, which is full of various techniques to calm yourself down and ground. You can customize goals, when they need accomplished (you can even set them months ahead), and if and when the app alerts you. It also offers “journeys”, where you choose a specific problem you want to work on, and it offers all kinds of goals you can choose to help you get in the habit. The best part is that once you finish a goal, your little bird grows, goes on adventures, earns you currency in the app, and even brings you gifts. You can use the currency to purchase clothing, decorations, etc. It really is a fun and satisfying way to organize your goals and hold yourself accountable. Please, get this. It’s 100% worth it. All of the concepts I just mentioned are free. The only thing you can’t do without purchase is specific soundscapes, clothes and decorations, prompts, and goals, which you can make for yourself in the add goals section if you really want it. I absolutely love this app, and have used it to be better for myself, in all aspects. You won’t regret downloading this app. It’s perfect in my opinion.

reviews.title: Dr. Recommended blend of self-care and life organizing
reviews.text: I had searched apps to help me with a healthy day flow but this one was recommended by my doctor! She uses it and gave me the tip when I said I was working in habits and mental health. Finch is able to seamlessly integrate wellbeing practices with life’s daily to do list. No other app allows you to stay on task and offer chances for deep reflection and emotional growth. You can grow through guiding your baby finch through staged of growth and by short burst of sharing your own experiences. The user interface is very easy to learn and explore. You can engage as much or as little as you want with the different app features. Some of my favorite features are the huge library of soundscapes, guided breathing exercises, and motivational quotes. Goals are easy to add and customize. You can also connect with others on Finch and offer encouragement and reminders. I wasn’t intent on using a “digital pet” app for my own life hacking but Finch is a category buster! The yearly subscription fee is reasonable. By the time my trial was over it was already so useful to me that I didn’t question paying for it. (Only downside: Their are some bugs in the auto tagging feature that “read” my reflections incorrectly. It categorized some items as negative when I meant the opposite. This is a small part of the experience, and only comes up in one section of your personalized weekly review. Again, you can toggle off the auto tag and the newsletter.)

reviews.title: One thing I would love to see changed…
reviews.text: Let me start by saying I love this App! It’s cute and motivating!! The way I use it is to stay focused on my very day tasks. So for instance, I can get pretty overwhelmed really fast especially since I have a physical disability, and I can’t stay focused to save my life. I start a task get distracted, and start a new one, so if I’ve been cleaning all day, but I never stayed focused on a task, it will seem like nothing got done. So on my app I have my entire day planned from start to finish. From the moment I wake up, get out of bed and brush my teeth, go do my tasks get ready to sleep and do it all over again. It’s literally all on the app. Now I’ve set everything up on my Journeys to make sure I’m keeping track on my process. My issue is that is that I can’t seem to get them to pop up on my goals for the day in order, so I have to sit there and move everything around to get my day started in order. I know it’s not a huge deal but it is time consuming and I get overwhelmed and distracted while moving everything around. I would really hope that in the future they could make it as in the journey goals for the day can have an order system for those of us that use the app like me. I think it would really be a game changer, instead of having to write down each day to get them to come on the goals section in order. That is literally my only issue, but again I love this app and I’m grateful to have it in my life!

reviews.title: I never expected this to work as well as it does
reviews.text: But it works! This app has done something I never thought would be possible for me: it has successfully incentivized me to be productive and compassionate with myself. I deal with anxiety and depression on a daily basis. It often makes it very difficult to do simple things like get out of bed and shower or leave the house. But all of this is becoming a lot easier since I downloaded this app! Finch has revolutionized my self-care process. I love the way that Finch characterizes my baby Bonbon. I feel like there is real thought and consideration put into certain actions like the little chats we have, as well as the constantly evolving customization options and the main mode of currency. It feels less like a to-do list and more like building a loving relationship with a Tamagotchi-like pet. It gamifies without feeling intrusive or resorting to micro transactions (though, they are there, along with a paid subscription option) At the end of the day, I know the company needs to make money, but everything about Finch—from its soft and comforting colors and characters, to its gentle messages and array of mindfulness/ self care options—genuinely feels tenderly designed and more indicative of human touch than I ever thought would be possible in a self-care app. I love this app. I love my baby Bonbon. I love getting virtual hugs from my friends. I’m so happy I downloaded this app after my friend sent me the invite.

reviews.title: My little lad!
reviews.text: Finch is a wonderful self care app. I got recommended it from a friend, and I really like it. I love how inclusive they are. I’m a non binary person who was raised in a community where pronouns were most commonly assumed to be masculine if the gender was unknown so having my finch be non binary and use they/them has helped me practice not misgendering people. I also really enjoy how simple the reflections are and how there are no consequences for forgetting to do something. Many self care apps will have you lose things for not checking in, and I find those more stressful than helpful. Overall, finch is a wonderful app! I think, however, finch could be improved with things like being able to write your own tasks. In the app, it suggests tasks for you to complete, as well as helps you create a daily schedule. However, it would be nice to additionally be able to write personalized tasks. Another issue is that they have an SOS page, but some days I can find it easily and others I have no clue where it went. I don’t personally need it too often but if I need time to relax and ground myself it can be frustrating when I can’t find it, and it could be dangerous for people who may need some of the more important SOS resources. Overall, finch is a great app. I highly recommend if to anyone who’s looking for something to help them start a self care routine. It can be as simple as being a little more grateful or as impactful as a full on exercise and dietary shift or change. Finch has got your back!

reviews.title: An excellent start to getting your life in order
reviews.text: I know it sounds corny, but it’s true. Before this app, I was spiraling. Deeply depressed, incredibly unorganized in both my home and my work, there was no aspect of my life that wasn’t filthy or miserable. Now I’m not saying this app single-handedly changed all that. But it put me on the right path towards changing it. I like to describe Finch as “a self-help-themed Tamagotchi”, the goal being to keep this baby bird alive and growing so you can do the same. While there’s no risk of killing your bird if you leave it without attention, you form a sweet little bond by giving it that attention. As you complete certain tasks you delegate yourself, the bird is given food to eat, giving it enough energy to go on adventures in the forest to tell you about. You can choose what you want to say back to her (you have to reply), whether it be choosing a set of options given to you or writing your own response. But no matter what you say, she does grow in certain traits. The way she talks to you will change, her personality will develop, etc.. You can also dress your bird up, decorate its home, among other things. You make friends with your pet bird while getting your life in order! What’s not to love? This app won’t be for everyone. And obviously, it didn’t fix my mental health by itself. But I’ll tell you this. Without it, I wouldn’t have ticked “find a therapist” off my to-do list. It got stuff done for me in a fun way, and I hope you’ll enjoy that same experience.

reviews.title: Best app ever!
reviews.text: With this app I’ve been able to stay remarkably consistent with my goals and self-care. Being able to buy clothes, colors, tickets to new locations, and furniture with the rainbow stones awarded for completing task has fueled me to stay on track more than anything I’ve tried before. Even more so, it is an amazing feature that the price for finch pro goes down as you stay consistent, thus offering a real financial benefit to your progress. The friends I’ve shared this app with were suspicious at first, either thinking they were too old to get any help from the app or too inconsistent to keep up with it, but now, they have continued to use it and all love it as much as I do. My finch is still growing, but using this app has grown me immensely too. I’ve become kinder to myself, more active, healthier, more confident, and found peace in the chaos of everyday life. Checking on my finch is a great escape and something I look forward to every day. I cannot thank the creators of finch enough, this app truly has changed my life. To any one who may think they’re too old for an app that follows a bird who goes on adventures or too inconsistent with their habits and goals to actually see any change, please try this app, you will not regret it. Truly I would have never guessed that my ADHD brain would be able to handle completing so many goals consistently, but it has worked beyond anything I could have imagined. Thank you Finch!

reviews.title: Hands down my favorite app
reviews.text: I started with Finch around 6 months ago because I have ADHD and I struggle with maintaining habits. Firstly they offer so much in the free version of the app- no limit to adding goals, reminders for them, categories to set up and sort into and goal ideas for you to explore. You can really personalize each goal or habit you put in. This alone but it above every other app I’ve tried like this. They also offer exercise ideas, breath work, gratitude practice, self love, and even more with very simple instructions and an easy app to navigate. Daily goals to remind you to explore these features and stay on top of your personal goals. An added bonus is the cute bird you’re taking care of, the adorable micro pets you collect, personalization of characters clothes and room, friends you can add and send things to (plus you are able to link goals with your friends to do together!) Lastly, you can travel to different locations in the app and each place has certain items for your bird to learn about. They’ll go on adventures and you chat with them afterwards, and I’ve found myself learning new things about the culture! This app is great if you have ADHD and struggle with habit formation and finishing tasks, it’s great for kids to keep track of habits and make new ones and I even have my mom on it every day learning more about loving herself and being gentle with herself! I would give 100 stars if I could, hats off to the creators for putting in so much work, knowledge, and making accessible to so many different people!

reviews.title: The best
reviews.text: I struggle with ADHD and the depression, anxiety, negative self esteem and burn out that comes with constantly having to fight just to survive. Baby steps? Easier said than done. The ADHD brain sees a mountain that needs to be climbed up all at once without even the proper equipment to do so. We can’t break things down. Other’s advice for us is not helpful because they don’t understand us and we end up feeling worse about ourselves. But Finch actually makes baby steps tangible, and gives you the incentive to reflect more on how you feel and actually see the progress you make. I can add and subtract my goals as I like, learn what is beneficial for me on my journey or what is not. It also helps you think about ways to reach out to others and consider about others feelings. I also love the exercises because I can do them from my couch! Even one minute of stretching is more than I would have otherwise and I can build up to more when I’m ready. You also get to know yourself more through the prompts and become more mindful. I’m using the free version and it is more than enough for me to get the benefits. I have more freeing of mental space because I can actually get things done that usually give me anxiety and it boosts my self esteem. I can learn to be more gentle on myself and more grateful with the help of the app. Maybe in the future I’ll buy the premium subscription to go deeper with my journey. But the free is perfect for the initial baby steps! Thanks so much to the creators for making this genius application.

reviews.title: Favorite App On My Phone! :))
reviews.text: Bro.. This app is a life saver. I could go on and on about how amazing this app is, and the focus it has on adding features that REALLY help the user, not just ones they think would look cool, or get the creators extra cash, etc. All the things you can do are so helpful in ways I didn’t even know I needed. Being able to send good vibes in different ways to friends has helped me stay in touch with people without realizing it, I’ve been finally reaching out to my friends using this app, asking about their Finch, how old they are, how much I like their outfits, etc. I’ve always struggled with communicating with my friends and not ghosting them randomly. This app has kept me connected to loved ones and motivated to do daily tasks. One feature I want to suggest adding, just because I think it’d be helpful, is a feature that lets you have separate tasks from your daily ones that stick around just until you complete them, such as finishing a certain movie one of these days, or finally buying that special item when you have time. We have activities you can set up to pop up DAILY in your journeys, and things you can set up JUST for tomorrow and then they’ll never show up again. But I want one that is daily, BUT gets rid of itself when I complete it without me having to delete it from my Journey. I’m bad at explaining, but it’d be nice :’) It’d be like a checklist for one-time only tasks, not daily tasks to help on your journey; but instead to help you remember things you need to complete once and not daily.

reviews.title: 5 Stars PERIOD!!!! PLEASE READ! BEST APP EVER!!!
reviews.text: This app is so fun I love it and since I got it I feel like I’ve been more productive and maybe even healthier. I love customizing my birb which is the pet u have in the app. Ur birb also has its own room and u can also customize ur birbs room. U can also customize its colors. The older u get the more u can change. U can also fly places once ur a child, like Paris, Maui, Galápagos Islands, Edinburgh, and more. In total there’s 24 destinations including the default one which is Finchie forest. U can also pet ur birb to increase ur friendship level with ur birb. U go on adventures, and every time u finish an adventure u discover something new. And every time u open the app it gives u an affirmation and asks u questions like in the morning it says “how motivated are u for today?” And in the afternoon it asks “how are u feeling?” And at night it asks “how satisfied are you with today?” And all u have to do is click a button to answer the questions. U can also have friends on finch like ur family members and friends in real life. And there’s no limit to how many friends you can have. And when u do have friends u can send them good vibes like hugs, gratitude, and more. I only explained probably only half of the things u can do on this app. This is definitely 5 Stars 🤩✨⭐️🌟🌠 (By the way this is an 11 year old writing this review. All my family members love this app including my siblings, grandparents, and parents.)
